findings.evidence: Mathlib defines `AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt` for an arbitrary ideal (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Frobenius.lean:54`). Here primality is only installed at lines 61/107 and never consumed, while `p` and `LiesOver` are used only at lines 62–83/108–110 to recover equality of contractions already implied by the `𝓞 K`-algebra equivalence.
findings.fix: State both for any ideal `Q`, and prove directly that mapping by the induced algebra equivalence preserves `Q.under (𝓞 K)`.
findings.issue: Both `isArithFrobAt_map_ringOfIntegersAlgEquiv` and its `_iff` version unnecessarily require `p`, `[Q.IsPrime]`, and `[Q.LiesOver p]`.

findings.evidence: The forward transport theorem at lines 36–49 needs only `[Q.IsPrime]`; in the iff proof, the sole uses of `p`/`LiesOver` are the unused local instance at line 142 and arguments needed only by the over-specialized Frobenius theorem.
findings.issue: `isUnramifiedAt_map_ringOfIntegersAlgEquiv_iff` unnecessarily takes `p` and `[Q.LiesOver p]`; neither belongs to unramifiedness transport.

summary: The transport statements impose unnecessary prime/fibre assumptions, preventing use at their natural level.
